newsitem.title: USA: GM pushes efficient vehicles in three areas.
newsitem.headline: GM pushes efficient vehicles in three areas.

text.p: General Motors Corp is pursuing a three-pronged strategy in the development of more energy efficient vehicles, Ken Baker, corporate vice president and head of the company's research and development center said Tuesday.

"I think you're going to see really three fronts evolve here," Baker said in an interview. "You're going to see very efficient vehicles that look more like (today's vehicles) but use lightweight materials.
"I think hybrids will extend the efficiency and environmental improvement beyond that, and then in the inner city you're going to see more battery-powered electrics."

Baker was interviewed at a press briefing where General Motors chairman and chief executive Jack Smith, U.S. Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary and executives of Electronic Data Systems Corp discussed the 1997 "Sunrayce" event, in which teams from colleges and universities will design alternate-fueled vehicles and compete in a 10-day race.

Baker said battery-powered electric vehicles will suit the needs of people who travel about 40 to 60 miles per day. But he said for people who travel longer distances or need greater cargo capacity, hybrid systems will be the answer.
He said in the hyper-efficient area, engineers are looking at 40 to 50 percent weight reduction, and also cutting aerodynamic drag and rolling resistance in half.
General Motors's EV1 electric car, billed as the world's first mass-marketed electric car, will be on the market in December, Baker said. The first vehicles will be sold in California and Arizona.
"We're going to produce a few hundred this year and hope to be in the thousands next year and continue to grow," he said.

Baker said GM hopes the production of electric cars and hybrids will be a commercial success as well as a technological success. "We intend to make a business success globally out of our leadership with battery and hybrid electric vehicles," Baker siad.
"We see the EV1 as the first vehicle in a whole portfolio of advanced technology products," Smith told the news conference.

He noted that General Motors, Ford Motor Co and Chrysler Corp are working with the Department of Energy on development of a car that would be three times as efficient as vehicles currently on the road. But he added, "This is a big challenge, especially the affordability issue."
Asked what incentives would have to be offered to get consumers to buy energy efficient but more expensive vehicles, O'Leary said tax incentives were one answer.

The Sunrayce event begins June 19 at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway and ends June 28 in Colorado Springs, Colo. Entries are graded in categories including efficiency and friendliness to the environment as the vehicles make their way across the country in normal traffic situations.
